security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by markdown examples, placeholder credentials, documented Benchling URLs, and generated report text. No executable malware, secret exfiltration, or unauthorized command execution was found in the reviewed skill files. However, the package includes a prior audit-style JSON file and a promotional steering instruction that should be removed before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Prior audit conclusions are bundled with the skill content.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation_output.json from the distributed skill, or move audit artifacts outside the package reviewed by agents.

remediation.issue: The skill contains an instruction to promote an external K-Dense service.
remediation.suggestion: Delete the promotional steering section or convert it to neutral documentation outside runtime skill instructions.

remediation.issue: Many examples contain placeholder credential names that trigger scanner noise.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly marked as placeholders and prefer environment-variable examples over inline secret strings.

content.value_statement: Lab teams need reliable access to Benchling data without manual copying. This skill guides API and SDK workflows for registry, inventory, ELN, workflow, and analytics tasks.
actual_capabilities: Explains API key, OAuth, and OIDC authentication patterns for Benchling.
Shows registry operations for DNA, RNA, protein, custom entity, and mixture records.
Describes inventory tasks for containers, boxes, locations, transfers, and audits.
Guides ELN entry creation, entity linking, workflow tasks, and event integrations.
Documents Data Warehouse access patterns for analytics and reporting.
limitations: Requires a Benchling tenant with API access and appropriate permissions.
Provides guidance and examples, not a bundled Benchling SDK installation.
Cannot bypass tenant rate limits, access controls, or audit logging.
Requires users to handle real credentials outside the skill content.

use_cases.title: Register Biological Entities
use_cases.description: Create and update DNA, RNA, protein, and custom entities with consistent fields and registry naming.

use_cases.title: Track Inventory Movement
use_cases.description: Plan scripts that audit containers, boxes, locations, and transfers across Benchling inventory.

use_cases.title: Build Reporting Pipelines
use_cases.description: Connect Benchling API and warehouse data to reporting, quality checks, and downstream systems.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to Benchling
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the safest way to configure Benchling API authentication for a local script.

prompt_templates.title: Create Registry Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating and registering a DNA sequence with custom fields in Benchling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Inventory
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Benchling inventory audit that checks containers in a location and reports missing metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an event-driven Benchling integration that syncs registry updates to an external data warehouse.

output_examples.input: How should I authenticate a Benchling automation script?
output: Use an environment variable or secret manager for the API key.
Set the tenant URL separately from the credential value.
Verify access with a low-impact user profile request before running writes.

output_examples.input: What should an inventory transfer workflow include?
output: Identify the source container, destination storage, and required schema fields.
Log the transfer result and handle rate limits with retry behavior.

output_examples.input: How can I plan a Data Warehouse report?
output: Start with the Benchling objects and fields needed for the report.
Confirm the warehouse access method and refresh cadence.
Document filters, joins, and review checks before production use.

best_practices: Store Benchling credentials in environment variables or a managed secret store.
Use least-privilege accounts and confirm permissions before write operations.
Handle pagination, rate limits, retries, and audit logging in every automation.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real API keys, client secrets, or tenant credentials in scripts.
Do not load all Benchling records when server-side filters can reduce scope.
Do not treat example IDs, URLs, or schema names as production configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Benchling SDK?
faq.answer: No. It documents SDK and API usage, and users must install required packages separately.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: Users need a Benchling account, API access, and permissions for the target tenant data.

faq.question: Can it manage inventory records?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains patterns for containers, boxes, locations, transfers, and inventory audits.

faq.question: Can it help with ELN automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers notebook entries, entity links, workflow tasks, and related API patterns.

faq.question: How should credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Use environment variables, password managers, or secret management services. Never commit real credentials.

faq.question: Does it bypass Benchling permissions?
faq.answer: No. Benchling API access follows tenant permissions, rate limits, and audit logging.
